title: Nothing in the brain resembles the sentence-like structure of beliefs

statements.text: Propositional attitudes have a sentential structure, discrete symbols and a combinatorial syntax, while the brain works by action potentials, spiking frequencies and spreading activation. It is hard to see where in the brain anything even remotely like a sentence could be found. The sentential attitudes play at best a limited and superficial role in cognition, and language is mainly a device for communication.

sources.locator: section 3.2.1, 'Challenging The Syntactic Structure Of Beliefs'
